## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Paṭhamabodhi Sutta* (Ud 1.1; PTS Ud 1) is the opening discourse of the *Bodhivagga* in the *Udāna* of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. It depicts the Buddha, immediately after his enlightenment under the Bodhi tree, contemplating specific conditionality (*idappaccayatā*) and dependent arising (*paṭiccasamuppāda*) in forward order [SuttaCentral]. Through this insight, the Buddha crystallizes the understanding that all experience arises conditioned by causes, fundamentally denying the existence of an unchanging essence or soul (*ātman*) [Runehov and Oviedo 2013]. The text is cited in early post-canonical exegetical works, including the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37) and the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 2.3) [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels listed by SuttaCentral include the awakening narrative of the Vinaya *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), the Sanskrit *Catuṣpariṣatsūtra* (SF 259), various recensions of the *Udānavarga* (UV 33, Uv Kg 33, UVS 33), and the *Mahāvastu* (San Lo Mvu 64), while closely resembling the companion discourses *Dutiyabodhi Sutta* (Ud 1.2) and *Tatiyabodhi Sutta* (Ud 1.3) [SuttaCentral]. Automatically computed text reuse matches from DharmaNexus confirm close Pali-internal reuse with the *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1) and the neighboring *Bodhi* discourses (Ud 1.2, Ud 1.3), along with extensive formulaic sharing with the *Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅga* (Vb 6), the *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12), and the *Mahātaṇhāsaṅkhaya Sutta* (MN 38) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language matches generated by DharmaNexus align the text with Sanskrit and Tibetan monastic and narrative accounts of the awakening, notably the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* (D0001-4) and *Abhiniṣkramaṇasūtra* (D0301), the Sanskrit *Saṅghabhedavastu*, and doctrinal citations in Candrakīrti's *Prasannapadā* and the *Lalitavistara* [DharmaNexus].
